title: Would Meatball Survive? Shorts v4 prototype (3 Shorts): animals that act
_note: Shorts v3 prototype (research/44). Same three animals as survive-01 (cassowary, boxjelly, badger) rewritten as Meatball-in-jeopardy stories: hook claim, he tries something, it goes wrong, the true fact is the punchline, twist/callback, loop line into the hook. Lines <= 8 words. Prototype voice: edge-tts Andrew at +0% then atempo 1.10 (= +10%); the final version would use Bill (vidiq voice, ~7 credits per Short). Photos: the same pinned, hand-checked iNaturalist observations as survive-01. Cassowary cut from 29.7 s to the 20-25 s window (coordinator 10/24: 20-22 s Shorts win): dropped 'On each foot.' and 'It jumps seven feet straight up.', shortened the droppings line and the loop line; every joke kept. | 10/24 ship pass (episodes/v3-01): cassowary 'Its poop plants rainforests.' -> 'Its poop plants trees.' (SD Zoo: many plants need passage through a cassowary to sprout; 'plants rainforests' overstated it); box jelly 'Australian first aid is vinegar.' -> 'First aid for this sting? Vinegar.' (ANZCOR: vinegar is for tropical/box jellyfish stings, not every Australian sting). Both re-rendered; the badger ships as the prototype render. Voice stays Andrew +10% (Nolan preferred it to Bill, 10/24; a Bill pass cost 14 vidIQ credits and was dropped).

beats.say: This bird has a four-inch dagger.
beats.short_title: I Tried to Befriend a Cassowary 🦶 (Would Meatball Survive?)
beats.bonus: Cassowaries also spread rainforest seeds: some only sprout after passing through one.
beats.comment: Would you get within kicking distance of this bird? 👇
sources: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, Cassowary fact page: 'dagger-like claw on the inner toe that is up to 4 inches (10 centimeters) long'; 'can slice open any predator or potential threat with a single swift kick'; 'run up to 31 miles per hour (50 kilometers per hour)'; 'jump nearly 7 feet (2 meters) straight up'; seeds of some rainforest plants 'much more likely to sprout after passing through a cassowary's digestive tract' — https://animals.sandiegozoo.org/animals/cassowary (checked 2026-10-24)
Mental Floss, 10 facts about cassowaries (mostly fruit; swallows fruit whole; disperses seeds) — https://www.mentalfloss.com/animals/birds/10-facts-about-cassowaries

beats.say: So naturally, I went to say hi.
It runs thirty-one miles an hour.
I can roll. Downhill. Sometimes.
One kick can slice open a threat.
Good news: it mostly eats fruit.
Bad news: it swallows fruit whole.
I'm round. I'm bite-sized.
Its poop plants trees.
Best case? I become a tree.
Would you get this close? Comment.
This jellyfish has twenty-four eyes.
beats.loop_say: Four of them are watching you. Because
beats.short_title: I Tried to Outsmart a Box Jellyfish 👀 (Would Meatball Survive?)
beats.bonus: Box jellyfish sting in Australia? Vinegar on the sting, then call emergency services (000). Vinegar stops unfired stingers; it is not a cure.
sources: Garm et al. 2011, Current Biology (24 eyes of four types; some with lenses; four always look up) — https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2011/04/110428123938.htm
Scientific American, 'Box Jellyfish Eyes Aim at the Trees' (no real brain) — https://www.scientificamerican.com/podcast/episode/box-jellyfish-eyes-aim-at-the-trees-11-04-29/

Chironex fleckeri: an untreated victim may die in two to five minutes (Wikipedia, citing Fenner 2005, Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chironex_fleckeri ; https://dhmjournal.com/images/IndividArticles/35June/Fenner_dhm.35.2.76-83.pdf

First aid: ANZCOR Guideline 9.4.5, Envenomation – Jellyfish Stings (tropical Australia: vinegar, then call 000) — https://www.anzcor.org/home/first-aid-management-of-injuries/guideline-9-4-5-envenomation-jellyfish-stings/
Photo note: no CC0/CC BY Chironex photo on iNaturalist; photos are other box jellyfish (Carybdea, Alatina, Copula), as in survive-01.

beats.say: And zero brains.
So I jumped in to outsmart it.
It doesn't need a brain.
Its tentacles are covered in stingers.
One brushed me. Just once.
One kind can stop a heart in minutes.
Good news: I don't have a heart.
First aid for this sting? Vinegar.
A meatball. In vinegar.
I'm a pickle now.
Would you swim there? Comment.
This badger is built to resist cobra venom.
beats.short_title: I Poked a Honey Badger 🦡 (Would Meatball Survive?)
beats.bonus: The same venom-blocking receptor change evolved separately in honey badgers, hedgehogs, pigs and mongooses.
beats.comment: Which animal would you least want to annoy? 👇
sources: Drabeck, Dean & Jansa 2015, Toxicon, 'Why the honey badger don't care: convergent evolution of venom-targeted nicotinic acetylcholine receptors' (honey badger, hedgehog, pig; mongoose known earlier) — https://experts.umn.edu/en/publications/why-the-honey-badger-dont-care-convergent-evolution-of-venom-targ/

Slate summary (receptor change blocks alpha-neurotoxin binding; resistance, not immunity) — https://www.slate.com/blogs/wild_things/2015/06/16/honey_badger_venom_resistance_biologists_discover_the_secret.html

Wikipedia, Honey badger: 'remarkably loose skin, allowing the badger to turn and twist freely within it'; eats snakes, scorpions; 'often raids beehives in search of both bee larvae and honey' — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honey_badger (checked 2026-10-24)

beats.say: A tiny change blocks part of the toxin.
So, obviously, I poked it.
It eats snakes. Scorpions. Bee larvae.
It rips open beehives for snacks.
It did not want to be friends.
Its skin is thick and super loose.
Grab it, and it twists around inside.
I'll be over here. Forever.
Hedgehogs evolved the same trick.
I evolved sauce.

_note_v4: Shorts v4 prototype (research/45): the v3-proto scripts, with the animal cut out whole and acting (beat "animal"), staged around Meatball. Cut-outs must be the whole animal (Nolan 10/25): photos whose animal runs off the photo's edge stay v3 stills. Where a joke needs the animal to act, the shot uses a photo whose whole animal is in frame: new pins found by scanning iNaturalist CC0/CC BY research-grade photos with the same cut-out check (cassowary 10749198, 324265024, 389877079, 142570937, 20345809; box jellyfish Copula sivickisi 144280380, 329960607, 154549857, 147738498, 83881186, 143334172, 327332202), checked by eye. Cassowary 'runs 31 mph': Meatball bolts off (run_off) while the bird lunges. Every photo whose animal runs off the photo's edge was replaced (Nolan 10/25), so every photo shot is a whole-animal cut-out. The two Alatina alata photos were dropped: one runs off the photo's edge, the other's matte breaks its tentacles into 9 pieces.
